**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**QUESTION 1: SUMMARY (15 marks)**

Read the following passage carefully and in two paragraphs of not more than 150 words, summarise it using your own words as far as possible.

National survey on Violence Against Children (VAC) in Nigeria determines three types of VAC to be physical violence, sexual violence and emotional violence. According to the study, out of the three VAC, sexual violence affects most number of children in Nigeria. Most respondents said they will report to the police when they witness violence against children in their community. In the same manner, as messengers of peace, we should not fold our arms at this menace. Rape is one of the crimes and social problems that is somewhat regarded as a community's least priority although the victims suffer from grave physical, mental, and emotional consequences. So, what is rape? Rape is a type of sexual assault usually involving having a carnal knowledge, which is initiated by one or more persons against another person without the person's consent. The act may be carried out by physical force, coercion, abuse of authority or against a person who is incapable of valid consent, such as one who is unconscious, incapacitated, or below the legal age of consent. The term rape is sometimes used interchangeably with the term sexual assault. The time is now and the place is anywhere in the world where this issue is not being given the attention that is warranted to fight the biasness towards rape victims. This can be witnessed in the recent social upheaval that has affected India whereby, a 23-year old paramedic student was gang raped, mauled and left to die naked in the streets of Delhi, the Indian capital. The incident generated widespread national and international coverage and was widely condemned, both in India and abroad.

The consequences of rape to the woman or man can be classified either as physically, mentally or emotionally traumatic. Among the physical effects include unwanted pregnancies, disease or health problems and certain disruptions on the natural bodily functions. On the other hand, psychological effects range from self-pity to the more striking suicidal tendencies. The most immediate physical effect of rape is the risk of the victim getting pregnant. Dependent on the age of the victim, she may conceive a child even if she has just reached puberty. In most instances, rape victims who become pregnant opt to abort the child that is considered the result of the crime committed against them. In some cases, the situation is further complicated due to abortions not being a legal option for the victim.

Without their knowledge, the rape victims are also at risk of acquiring sexually transmitted diseases such as HIV/AIDS that could affect their health in the short and long term even leading to death. Since rape is a form of forced intercourse, the victim's body usually suffers physical injury particularly to the vagina, uterus, and other parts of the reproductive system. The risks are greater if the rape victim is a child or a very young teen. In addition, the rape victims are often beaten up and tortured during and after the rape which might even lead to losing their lives in some cases. The foremost psychological effect of rape will be emotional trauma and paranoia. At times, the victim will exhibit symptoms of mental and emotional trauma through solitude and exclusion. They also develop fear in mingling and socializing with strangers and other people especially men. These effects can last for the duration of the victim's lifetime. Apart from making her aloof and isolated, rape can also lead the victim to pity or self-blame for the crime. This effect is partly caused by the social stigma or shame that societies or communities wrongly attribute to the victim. She is often deprived of the care she should receive from families and society at large, who in turn can accuse her of callous and provoking behaviour. This worsens her mental state and she is emotionally devastated for life. The most striking effect that rape can produce in a victim is the tendency of the thought of committing suicide. Because of trauma, self-pity and seclusion, rape victims often feel that there is no longer hope and they could no longer recover and that they are not worthy of living. It is time that all humans demand change in all countries that perpetrate such injustices world-wide. It is time to provide the education and information and encourage discussions that will change society's attitudes towards rape and find ways to eradicate this intolerable social issue once and for all.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model summary (120 words, two paragraphs)**

A Nigerian survey found that sexual violence is the most widespread form of violence against children, yet communities give rape little priority although victims suffer greatly. Rape is sexual contact imposed without consent, by force, coercion or abuse of authority, or on someone unable to consent. The widely condemned gang attack on a student in Delhi shows how seriously the world can react.

The effects are physical and psychological. Victims risk unwanted pregnancy, sexually transmitted diseases, injuries and sometimes death. They suffer trauma, fear of others, isolation and self-blame, worsened by stigma and the lack of family support, which can drive them to suicide. Society must therefore educate people, encourage open discussion and change attitudes in order to eradicate rape.

**Content points expected**

1. A Nigerian survey identifies three types of violence against children (physical, sexual, emotional); sexual violence affects most children.
2. Rape is sexual assault without consent, by force, coercion or abuse of authority, or against a person who cannot consent (unconscious, incapacitated, under age).
3. The issue is a community's least priority although victims suffer greatly; the Delhi gang attack caused national and international condemnation.
4. Physical effects: unwanted pregnancy (and abortion, sometimes illegal), sexually transmitted diseases such as HIV/AIDS, injuries to the reproductive system, beating and torture that can kill.
5. Psychological effects: trauma, paranoia, fear of strangers and men, isolation, self-blame, made worse by stigma and the lack of family and social support; suicidal thoughts and hopelessness.
6. Society must demand change, educate people, encourage discussion, change attitudes and eradicate the problem.

**Marking grid (indicative; the paper prints 15 marks but not their split)**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Content | The main points above, accurate and in a logical order, without examples and details |
| Own words | Rephrasing of the passage ('imposed without consent' for 'initiated ... without the person's consent'), not copied strings |
| Expression and accuracy | Exactly two paragraphs, 150 words at most, correct grammar and linking words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying whole sentences from the passage, or lifting the statistics and the Delhi details at length.
2. Exceeding 150 words, writing one paragraph or three, or adding personal comments.
